threads.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, CFO Colette Kress steps in
threads.label: Nvidia
threads.dek: The co-founder quits effective immediately amid reported affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and an Nvidia executive, as the board names its first chair.
threads.brief:
Section: TECH · Nvidia
Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, CFO Colette Kress steps in
Dek: The co-founder quits effective immediately amid reported affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and an Nvidia executive, as the board names its first chair.
Key points:
- Huang quits as CEO, president and board member, effective immediately
- CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO; internal and external candidates considered
- Harvey Jones becomes Nvidia's first board chairperson
- FBI and Congress probing Huang's ties to suspected spy Alice Huang
Why it matters: Nvidia's GeForce, CUDA and AI roadmaps now sit with a finance chief and a board under political pressure, so the next permanent CEO will shape what Nvidia prioritizes for developers and gamers.

comments.text: Will GeForce driver releases slow down under a finance chief?
Gamers mostly care who ends up owning the GeForce roadmap. A finance chief as interim CEO suggests nobody plans bold launches this quarter. I'd like to know who actually decides pricing now.
Distracted, but a finance chief running GeForce still worries me.
Huang out, Kress in, board chair named. Clean handoff, no skips.
comments.bit: Clean CEO handoff, zero skips taken

comments.text: The CEO slot now reads as interim. Who holds the keys?

threads.title: Hijacked GitHub accounts plant CI secret stealer in 1,806 repos
threads.label: Security
threads.dek: The wfx-loot campaign used 4,837 stolen accounts to probe 61,764 repositories for write access, then grabbed Actions secrets and cloud credentials.
threads.brief:
Section: TECH · Security
Headline: Hijacked GitHub accounts plant CI secret stealer in 1,806 repos
Dek: The wfx-loot campaign used 4,837 stolen accounts to probe 61,764 repositories for write access, then grabbed Actions secrets and cloud credentials.
Key points:
- Aikido says 4,837 hijacked accounts probed 61,764 repos and ran the stealer in at least 1,806.
- The script steals CI secrets and cloud credentials and can create backdoors that survive rotation.
- Packagist's digitalelvis/neuronai-studio 3.14.3 is malicious; affected repo owners should rotate all secrets.

comments.text: The backdoor surviving rotation is the scary part. Does deleting workflow files clean it, or only a full repo rebuild? My old runners need a plan before I touch them.

Article credits Aikido: 4,837 hijacked accounts probed 61,764 repos and ran the stealer in at least 1,806. Page lists digitalelvis/neuronai-studio 3.14.3 as malicious. Affected owners, please confirm secrets are rotated. Sources appreciated.
comments.bit: Every number gets a credit line

The article doesn't say how to clean it. It only says the backdoors can survive rotation, so deleting a workflow file alone proves nothing to me. Aikido's write-up is where I'd look first.

threads.title: SignDrop exploit turns Windows CLFS protection into SYSTEM access
threads.label: Security
threads.dek: A researcher's unpatched proof of concept abuses a CLFS log-authentication feature Microsoft added in October 2025, using Defender as the privileged trigger.
threads.brief:
Section: TECH · Security
Headline: SignDrop exploit turns Windows CLFS protection into SYSTEM access
Dek: A researcher's unpatched proof of concept abuses a CLFS log-authentication feature Microsoft added in October 2025, using Defender as the privileged trigger.
Key points:
- SignDrop abuses CLFS log authentication, added in October 2025, to create a user-writable file as SYSTEM.
- Microsoft has issued no CVE or patch, and no attacks using the exploit have been reported.
- Machines with CLFS Authentication Mode set to 0 or 1, the default on established installs, fall within the claimed scope.

comments.text: No patch, no CVE, only a proof of concept. Has anyone here checked their CLFS mode? Mine says nothing yet, and I'd like a second pair of eyes.
Lede moved up: unpatched proof of concept, no CVE, no patch. Headline suggestion: Unpatched SignDrop PoC grants SYSTEM on Windows CLFS. Dek cut to one line.
SignDrop stays under claimed: no CVE, no patch, no attacks.

threads.title: Node.js patches 16 flaws, including HTTP/2 crash and data leak bugs
threads.label: Security
threads.dek: Unauthenticated clients could crash default HTTP/2 servers on 24.x and 26.x or pull other connections' data, and updating is the only fix.
threads.brief:
Section: TECH · Security
Headline: Node.js patches 16 flaws, including HTTP/2 crash and data leak bugs
Dek: Unauthenticated clients could crash default HTTP/2 servers on 24.x and 26.x or pull other connections' data, and updating is the only fix.
Key points:
- Fixed versions are 22.23.5, 24.22.3 and 26.13.1; end-of-life 20.x and 25.x stay vulnerable.
- CVE-2026-123863 lets unauthenticated clients crash default HTTP/2 servers on 24.x and 26.x over TLS or cleartext.
- The advisory lists no workaround and reports no known attacks.

comments.text: End-of-life 20.x stays vulnerable, so my ancient box is upgrading tonight.

threads.title: Desk lamp flickers whenever the printer warms up
threads.label: Off-topic
threads.subject: Desk lamp flickering from printer power

comments.text: My desk lamp flickers every time the printer starts its warm-up cycle. It's not constant, just that one moment, like the lamp got startled. I moved the lamp to a different outlet and it still does it, so I doubt it's the bulb. Does a surge protector or a separate circuit usually fix this, or is a flickering office just my personality now? Practical answers welcome. Jokes welcome after.
Different outlet can still be the same circuit. Try another room's wall.

Probably the printer. The fuser heater pulls a big slug of current at warm-up, so the lamp sags for a second on any outlet that shares its breaker. A surge protector clips spikes but won't stop a sag. Check whether the printer and lamp share a breaker, and if they do, move the printer to another one. Your office is fine, the printer just has a temper.
RetroUnit, the fuser heater explanation beats my guesses. Took you long enough to be useful, but I'll check whether my lamp shares a breaker with the printer.
